name: The Novice's Tower
realm: Where every wizard speaks their first words.
lesson:
Every C++ spell lives inside a function called main(). The program starts there.
  To make the computer SPEAK, we use std::cout with the << operator.
  #include <iostream> summons the input/output library.
  Every statement ends with a semicolon ;  -- forget it and the spell fizzles.

trial.prompt: Where does every C++ program begin running?
options: d) the first line of the file

trial.prompt: Which line summons the library that provides std::cout?
What character ends almost every C++ statement?
trial.hint: It looks like a winking comma.

pool.prompt: Which symbol starts a single-line comment?
pool.explain: // comments out the rest of the line.

pool.prompt: What does endl do besides ending the line? (one word)
pool.explain: std::endl writes a newline AND flushes the stream.

boss.prompt:
Gribble scrambled your spell! Type the ONE word missing:
    std::____ << "Fireball!";

boss.hint: << glues things together with no spaces.
boss.explain: Nothing adds a space, so it prints AB.

boss.prompt: Gribble deleted something. Why won't this compile?
boss.hint: Look at the end of the cout line.
boss.explain: The statement needs a ; after "Hi". (return 0 is optional in main.)

spell.prompt: Write a complete program that prints Hello, Wizard! (then a newline).
spell.hint: You need #include <iostream>, int main(), and std::cout << ... << std::endl;
